brief: Hawkish rate expectations are already priced into bonds: US and European rates have sold off over 80bp this year, with pricing implying at least 100bp of further Fed tightening and 125bp total from the ECB. Despite this, Goldman estimates systematic trend-following investors are short approximately $171 million of global bond DV01, the largest short since April 2026 and comparable only to February 2022 before that. The largest relative shorts are in Japanese and European rates, with US shorts including the five-year sector. Because systematic investors follow price trends, a pause in the yield rise, not a rate cut, could force short covering and amplify a rally. Potential triggers: oil stabilizing, softer inflation data, or central banks delivering already-priced tightening without a new hawkish surprise. The document favors expressing this as a tactical belly-of-the-curve trade (an IEF Oct 91.5/94 call spread) rather than long-dated TLT, and frames it as a positioning unwind, not a structural bond bull market. Renewed highs in oil, inflation expectations, or the five-year yield would invalidate the thesis.
